title: Purity of ordinary cohomology
statement:
In the situation of [prop-weight-purity], for every
$0\leq i\leq2d$ the
Frobenius module
$H^i(X,\Qlb)$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$.

proof.text: Use exactly the finite-field datum, prime $\ell\ne p$, coefficient field $\Qlb$, isomorphism $\iota$, smooth proper geometrically connected scheme $X_0$ of pure dimension $d$, geometric fiber $X$, and global geometric Frobenius fixed in the situation of the statement. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-smooth-proper-purity-hypotheses] applies to this datum and shows that both $H^j(X,\Qlb)$ and $H_c^j(X,\Qlb)$ are finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces with the induced global geometric-Frobenius actions, for every integer $j$. These supply the finiteness and action requirements used in Step 2; no finiteness assumption is added to the item.

source.place: Proof, application of clause (4) of thm-weil-deligne-purity; explicit verification of its hypotheses

proof.text: Fix any integer $i$ with $0\le i\le2d$. Apply [thm-weil-deligne-purity] to the same $p,a,q,k_0,k,\ell,\Qlb,\iota,X_0,X,d$ and the same global geometric Frobenius. Its smoothness, properness, geometric connectedness and pure-dimension hypotheses are those in the situation of the statement. The exceptional-adjoint admissibility, the chosen dualizing Weil complex with underlying object $Ra_X^!\Qlb$, and its canonical functorial Weil lift are also already assumed in that situation. Step 1 supplies finite-dimensionality of all the displayed cohomology groups. Thus every hypothesis of the theorem holds. Project its fourth conclusion: $(H^i(X,\Qlb),F_{\Qlb})$ is $\iota$-pure of weight $i$. This is precisely the finite-dimensional Frobenius-module weight predicate of [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], with the same coefficient isomorphism $\iota$ and base $q$. Since $i$ was arbitrary in the required interval, the assertion follows.

The statement is verbatim the same in the master and main-20261015 blueprints, and both proofs consist of one sentence: clause (4) of thm-weil-deligne-purity. Step 1: lem-weil-smooth-proper-purity-hypotheses clause (3) is in the same unit. Its hypotheses (finite-field datum, l!=p, the algebraically closed Qlbar coefficient category, X0 smooth, proper, geometrically connected of pure dimension d) are exactly the ones fixed in prop-weight-purity. It gives finite-dimensional H^i and H^i_c for every i, which discharges the theorem's explicit finiteness hypothesis that the blueprint's one-sentence proof leaves unstated. Step 2: I checked every hypothesis of thm-weil-deligne-purity against prop-weight-purity: p, a, q, k0, k, l, Qlbar, iota, X0, X, d, g_X, the constant Weil object on the small pro-etale site, admissibility, and the dualizing Weil complex with For(omega)=Ra^!Qlbar and its canonical Weil lift. All of them are present. The cohomology conventions agree: RGamma=Fib_s(Ra_*), per def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology. F_Qlbar, the scalar extension of F_l, is the same as the theorem's induced operator, because def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius defines the operator only at finite stages and def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients builds Qlbar objects from finite stages. Clause (4) is exactly the def-weil-frobenius-module-weights predicate with the same q and iota. That definition belongs to another unit but is only a notion, so the route stays in unit sk-input-weights, as in the unit's own proof of clauses (4)-(5). No tool_uses, no SGA. A read-only traversal finds no cycle; the only node that cites the item is prop-weight-purity-roots. cor-zl-purity-smooth-proper is a strict generalization in another unit, not a duplicate, so same_as=[] is defensible. Small cases check out: d=0 (H^0=Qlbar with F=id), i=2d (eigenvalue q^d), an elliptic curve with i=1 (Hasse bound), and zero groups (the condition holds vacuously). proof_deps is exactly the union of the steps' uses; the one added stmt_dep, def-weil-frobenius-module-weights, is correct. delivery-errors A-F all pass.
